issues.description: The gloss for 'jeans' ('strong blue clothes for your legs, usually long') is slightly imprecise: jeans are not always blue, and 'usually long' implies short jeans are common (short denim ones are 'shorts', not jeans). 'Clothes' (plural) for a single garment is also a little loose.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the gloss to: 'trousers made of strong cloth, usually blue' — 'trousers' is known at A2 and this is accurate and simpler.

issues.description: The grammar note says superlatives 'say one thing is the best in a group', but 'the cheapest' does not mean 'the best'; a superlative means something has the most of a quality in a group. A learner could wrongly equate superlative with 'good'.
issues.suggested_fix: Rephrase to: 'Superlatives like "the cheapest" say one thing is number one in a group (the most or the least of something).'

qa_report.summary: All four dialogue lines are grammatical, natural and firmly A2, and the clip correctly demonstrates both a comparative ('warmer than') and a superlative ('the cheapest') as the spec requires. Reference is consistent throughout ('they'/'them'/'ones' all point back to 'jeans'). Only two minor imprecisions: the 'jeans' gloss overstates 'blue' and oddly adds 'usually long', and the grammar note loosely equates superlatives with 'the best'. Neither would teach anything seriously wrong, so this can be approved, ideally with the suggested small wording fixes.
